recs.name: Together Aboard
recs.tag: It isn't a fear of the elements that stops her heading for faraway places.

lines.x: Rhodes Island Bioengineering Lab
10:00 A.M. \ Sunny, clear
Weedy?
Oh, sorry, sorry.
I used the disinfectant spray at the door... and I wasn't doing any experiments before I came...
I'm coming in, okay? I don't wanna hear any whining that I smell like machine oil this time.
Anyway, your contract's almost up, and they make us do an interview before we can renew it. I brought the draft for the new one.
Not much has changed, really; just trying to get HR off my back.
Hello? Anybody home?
Dang, I forgot. Weedy and Blaze always do physical training at this hour. Guess I'm off to the training grounds.
Over here, Luli.
Sorry I'm late. I almost didn't recognize you.
Is that so? Speaking of which, if I didn't know any better I'd think you were born and raised in Columbia.
I have spent an awful long time in Trimounts, after all. We haven't seen each other since Iberia, have we?
I was in the audience when you gave Rhine Lab's presentation at the last Trimounts Bioengineering Frontier Conference.
Really?
I was going to meet you after the session, but I had to leave for an emergency call from the Medical Department.
So you were the Rhodes Island representative who had to withdraw?
We'd just taken in a batch of patients in critical condition, and they needed my expertise.
You do realize how competitive that conference is, don't you? There are so many universities and tech companies fighting for those slots.
Spike the temperature to herd the enemy where you want them, then finish 'em off with the chainsaw.
Hyah!
Blaze! Got a moment?
Hey, Closure. How'd you like my move just now?
Spicy. It's just you here, though? Where's Weedy?
We cancelled today's training.
Huh? Why?
I thought it was about yesterday at first.
Yesterday, huh...?
Careful!
At these temperatures—
No need to hold back. I want to test the limits of the water cannon post-modification.
Can you take the recoil though?
Should be fine. It's a chance to put that physical training to the test.
Alright then.
Get ready, Leaf!
What...? Did you... knock her out?!
No! Nothing to do with that! She cancelled to go see an old friend.
Oh yeah?
A Rhine Lab employee, apparently.
She never told me about that...
Wait, Rhine Lab?! And that didn't raise any alarm bells for you?!
(Shakes head)
Weedy was one of the first to join Rhodes Island, her contract's about to expire, and I've been trying in vain to track her down these past few days.
And now she's meeting with an old buddy from Rhine Lab.
On top of all that, just the other day she got injured while training with a certain someone.
Hey, she wasn't injured! I know it looked bad, but I took her to Medical for a full checkup.
Either way, all signs point to...
No way.
I sure hope not.
Seriously, why would you swing for the fences in training? Don't you know how strong you are?
Weedy knocked me back too, you know... She's gotten a lot stronger and more skilled.
Excuse me, miss.
Could you please move this, er... gun? It's blocking the passageway.
Oh, sorry about that.
Thank you.
What's that, Weedy?
It's a water cannon that can shoot water at various pressures, or even as high-temperature steam jets.
It can be used as a portable energy source, which is useful for localized testing of the landship's automation upgrades.
Looks more like a weapon to me. That shoots people with high-pressure water jets. Or steam, apparently.
Well, yes, combat was another application it was designed for.
Researchers need weapons too.
Why on Terra would the head of Rhodes Island's bioengineering lab ever have to fight? Do they not assign security forces for their researchers?
That's not what I meant.
I had the idea of building a water cannon back when I was still in Iberia.

lines.st: When the Inquisition came to Abuelo's lab.
They confiscated all his documents and materials.
My grandfather's life's work, what would have been the first thesis in Iberia, indeed in all Terra, to detail the changes in the ocean from a combined biological and engineering perspective.
Abuelo's research license was suspended. All further research was subject to direct review by the Inquisition.

lines.x: I would sometimes wonder, could I have blasted them out of his lab if I'd had a weapon like this back then?
You'd need more than a water cannon to deal with the Inquisition.
Yes, it was just the fancy of a child. That's why I mostly use it for construction and development.
Oops, I almost forgot we had business to attend to.
You were looking for me, Closure?
Is your boss back yet?
No. Weedy went—
Yeah, I know. I didn't see her at the lab.
The bioengineering lab is out of service right now.
Huh?
Don't you remember? You came in without disinfecting last time, causing the contamination detection alarm to go off and—
Hey, I cleaned up right away, didn't I?
Yes, you used one of the hand-wash stations, putting the entire water sanitation system out of commission.
It's not my fault Weedy turned the detection AI's sensitivity all the way up!
Regardless, she decided to fully disinfect the lab and let it idle for a week before reopening it.
Someday we'll need to have a talk about how her mysophobia intersects with laboratory regulations.
Wait, but won't that delay your latest project?
Didn't Weedy submit a bunch of reports and funding applications just last week?
Oh, crap, I think I forgot to approve them...
Weapon upgrades for the training grounds... procurement for the Logistics Department... bridge repairs...
I could swear I left them right here.
Crap, don't tell me I misplaced her applications.
Lab out of service, new projects not getting approved... She must be tearing her hair out by now. Do you know what she's been up to lately?
She received a package that seemed to contain some kind of research materials from an old friend. She's been going over them in her quarters.
An old friend? The same one who works for Rhine Lab? The one she's meeting today?
Yes, that one.
So she's already helping other companies with their projects.
Huh?
She's already made up her mind then...
Oh jeez, how am I going to explain this to Kal'tsit and Amiya?
Come to think of it, she's had a hand in half of Rhodes Island's automation projects...
She's one of our oldest employees, but never gets the attention she deserves. Can't blame her for keeping her resume up-to-date.
Heck, the only reason she came here in the first place is that we were the first to make an offer.
I've failed her as both a supervisor and a colleague...
What are you talking about, Closure?
Do you know where Weedy is meeting her friend?
A bar, I think.
Oops, I almost forgot we had business to attend to.
I've looked through the documents you sent me.
Specifically, I made some corrections to the section on beachfront engineering based on Ægir technology, referencing the models and theories from Abuelo's manuscripts.
Thanks, Weedy. You're the only one I could think of when it comes to this stuff.
Rhine Lab has experts on all sorts of things, but not on the ocean or the Ægir.
No problem, it was nothing.
I've been away from Iberia for a while, though, so there might be new variables I haven't taken into account. I can't guarantee 100% accuracy.
That's fine, I'll cross-check them in the field. I just wanted to gather all the materials I could pertaining to the current state of research, before I go back to Iberia.
You're going back to Iberia?!
Why so suddenly?
I was visited by a Messenger from the Inquisition last month.
The Inquisition...
They brought a research proposal on maritime engineering, a handwritten letter from an Inquisitor, and an entrance permit into Iberia issued by the Inquisition.
The documents you went over were part of that research.
So they're opening up research into the ocean to outsiders...
Yes. Iberia is seeking change.
Have you made up your mind?
Yes, that one.
But you've spent so much time at Rhine Lab.
I'll be turning in my resignation. There's a lot of red tape involved, though. Project handovers, non-compete clauses, etc. Exactly what you'd expect from a big company.
But Iberia is in my blood. No matter how far away I go, I'll always smell the scent of brine in the air, and follow it back to Iberia.
There were two reasons I came here. The first was to hand over the responsibilities of the Rhine Lab liaison. The second was to seek you out.
You want me to come back to Iberia with you.
Yes.
I'm sorry, Luli, but I can't.
Because of Rhodes Island?
Forgive me for being frank, but Rhodes Island is hardly the ideal employer.
Due to their focus on clinical application, and involvement in crises across Terra, the resources they can offer for your research are limited.
And not only did they make you pull out of the Trimounts Bioengineering Frontier Conference, apparently you have to fill in for armed personnel?
Well, as I've already explained—
Your contract with them is about to expire, too.
Rhodes Island isn't what you think it is, Luli.
You still have chip on your shoulder about Iberia, don't you? Because of what happened to your grandfather?
Didn't you use to say that 'limitations on science are always set by people'?
Those were Abuelo's words. I tried very hard to convince him to leave Iberia, but he never did.
Science is the exploration of the unknown, but those who passionately throw themselves into it will find many locked drawers in front of them. The ocean, the Ægir, the Profound Silence...
No researcher could possibly enjoy an Iberia like that.
But Weedy, the tide has come ashore, reaching up to Iberia's ankles, and threatens to drown all of it.
So I've heard from our newer Iberian operators.
We can demand that the Inquisition release your grandfather's research. After all, it's closely linked to the maritime engineering project they sent over.
Iberia needs to seek change. The locks on those drawers are opening up, one by one.
I know.
But I can't go back with you right now.
Why not?
For the reason you brought up before tossing it aside: I need to stay at Rhodes Island.
Abuelo hated Iberia, and he hated the Inquisition, for laying waste to his life's work in an instant.
But he wouldn't leave the country, even after his research license was revoked.
I thought it was because he was old and didn't feel like going through the effort of starting over.
But there's no such thing as a utopia for scientific freedom. Far too many scientists have died in exile.
Later, I began to understand that he simply wanted to keep defending what he loved doing. He was waiting for the locks to open, to pick his research back up.

lines.st: Science is the exploration of the unknown, Weedy.
There will always be blanks, and places that are off-limits.
One blank gets filled in, and another appears. The frontiers are endless.
And no matter where you go, there will always be somewhere off-limits.
Limitations on science are always set by people, but it's also people who break those restraints. Passionate people.

lines.x: Congratulations. You passed our tests. Welcome to the team.
You say tests... It was one interview.
Eh, we're a start-up. We need all the talent we can get.
It took a lot of convincing to get Amiya to set up a bioengineering lab. You're the only member right now, so we're counting on you to make something of it! No pressure.

Of course, we'll give you all the support we can, in terms of funding, equipment, experiments... Anything you need, just say the word.
Just one thing... do you think we could negotiate on your requirement to wash our hands an average of 10 times every 3 hours?
Hey, what's with that look on your face?
The operation went well.
Great.
It's all thanks to your help fixing the sickbay's automation equipment.
I'm really sorry we had to call you back like this. That was an important conference, wasn't it? You spent so much time on that thesis.
It's okay. All five Infected are out of danger, right?
Yes.
Good.
By the way, there's a child who wants to chat with your bionic seadragon. She says you promised her before the operation.
Right. I'll head in now.
Are you sure? You must be tired.
Sorry, I should've been more careful. You hurt anywhere?
I'm fine.
You could just focus on your experiments, you know.
Weren't you the one who said I needed to build up my constitution?
What I mean is you don't have to fight.
Surgery and experiments can solve only a small part of the Oripathy problem, as—
Enough lectures, sheesh. Just stay behind me, alright? The battlefield can be chaotic, but I'll take out all the enemies before you're in any danger.
Don't underestimate an industrial water cannon.
I'm staying at Rhodes Island for the same reason that Abuelo wouldn't leave his lab, and the same reason you've chosen to return to Iberia.
It's not because I'm afraid of restrictions in a far-away land, but because there's something here that I'm passionate about, which I feel is important to carry on.
Excuse me, miss...
Closure?!
Please Weedy, won't you reconsider?
Reconsider... what?
You know how excited Blaze gets in battle. She didn't mean it.
And you know I get a little hare-brained when things get busy.
I didn't reject those funding applications you sent last week, I just misplaced them!
Heck, I still remember the titles! 'Connecting Heterogenous Arts Units,' 'Reengineering Ægir Maritime Technology Through Lighthouse Components'... they have a lot of potential.
(Maritime technology...)
Misplaced?
You signed them on the spot and handed them back to me. Did you forget?
Oh... Well, anyway, I want you to give serious consideration to staying at Rhodes Island.
Er... did you think I was going to leave?
HR was pressing me to get your contract renewal done, but I just couldn't find you. You weren't at the lab, either.
Luli's going back to Iberia, so I came to see her off. Oh, I forgot. This is Luli, from Rhine Lab.
About to resign from Rhine Lab, actually. I'm Luli. Let's just say Weedy and I are fellow countrymen.
Resign? So you're not...?
Ahem. I'm Closure, head of Rhodes Island's Engineering Department, and Weedy's supervisor and friend.
I'm not interrupting anything, am I?
No, we were just about done.
I think I understand your choice, Weedy. I'll respect it.
And it looks like you do plan to...
Right, just not now. Thanks for coming to see me. Have a safe trip.
Bye bye.
Bye.
Wait, you said you went into the bioengineering lab today?
...Er, yeah.
Didn't you know it needed to be put into idle cycle for a week after being disinfected?
Closure!

recs.name: The Sea Breeze on the Salt Flat
recs.tag: She pushes open the door of the past, and finds someone who still lingers within.

lines.x: Ahem... Here we are, Señorita Weedy.
This vehicle is used by the Inquisition to transfer documents between courts. It will not be under much scrutiny. The official letters I gave you should ensure safe passage.
The coachman can be trusted, but the best he can do for you is pretend to take a nap as you pass through the borderlands...
Take this money too. It's what little savings I have left, after all's said and done. It should come in handy on your way back to Rhodes Island.
You...
Go. Remember, you never saw me, and never visited the Salt Flat or Aarón. You've never returned to Iberia since you left...
And once you're gone, never return again.
Two days ago
We're here, Señorita Weedy.
...I thought a handover involving Iberia, Ægir, and Rhodes Island would be taking place more openly, like the lighthouse that has been relit.
I see. So the Inquisition is concerned about me.
You're clever.
Rhodes Island will hand over the Catastrophe warning system and medical center core components to the two Ægir consuls...
Neither Iberia nor Ægir will keep official records of this handover. As such, it would be inconvenient for either Irene or Secunda to attend.
And as a Rhodes Island operator who happens to be in Iberia, no one would be more qualified to oversee the handover. However—
'However, you're suspected of associating with bandits and interfering with the Inquisition's administration of justice at Aarón'?
Or is it, 'starting with your grandfather, your entire family are considered criminals by the Inquisition'?
No need to be so guarded. That era is in the past.
But it remains the recent past, and some degree of vetting is still required.
I expect you're familiar with this building?
Abuelo's old bionic lab.
The Inquisition has sent all records associated with the Penia family's research here. Please review them so that we may archive them.
Then, you may begin the handover.
The accumulated records are quite voluminous. I've assigned a clerk to assist you... I'm sure he'll be of help.
Someone who could help...
Once you see him, I'm sure you'll understand that the Inquisition is acting in good faith.
Mm—*cough* *cough*.
I forgot you were allergic to dust... I should've cleaned the place. It's been in disuse for many years.
I often saw you when I visited Abuelo here, Señor Callisto. Weren't you even more obsessed with cleanliness than I was?
Abuelo used to joke that your obsession with it was the only thing keeping you First Research Secretary, instead of taking his job.
Well, nowadays this old man is no more than a low-level clerk in the Inquisition, Señorita Weedy.
If it weren't for my familiarity with these records, I wouldn't have even had the chance to leave my office... if you can call it that.
So, how did you end up...
L-Let's not talk about that, Señorita. We should begin.
The Inquisition won't be giving either of us much time.
Alright.
This is the writ of sealing for the five bionic labs associated with the Penia family, one of which we're standing in right now. Please sign the last page once you've reviewed it.
...Alright.
This is the notice of destruction of the relevant equipment. Please sign it too.
Alright.
This is... there's a lot of it.
I remember all these models and formulae...
Counting both published and unpublished, the Penia family has written a total of... 3782 papers on bionic science.
What you're holding are the originals. All other extant copies have been destroyed.
If you stacked them up, the originals alone must be almost as tall as I am... This must represent decades of work for Abuelo and the rest of you.
After the Profound Silence, the Inquisition terminated all sea-related research in Iberia, but Señor Penia's bionics project went on until just a decade ago...
Compared to the thousands of projects snuffed out by the Inquisitors virtually overnight, we were the lucky ones.
Do you really think so?
...Another one, Señorita Weedy. Just sign on the last page if there's no issue.
In the derelict lab, the old man buries himself in the mountain of records, taking out paper after paper, summarizing them, then handing them over to Weedy.
His head is bowed, and Weedy cannot see his expression.
Is this how all old clerks end up, once their personalities are worn away by years of mundane work?
Quiet, rigid, patient, refusing to communicate outside of work, unemotional... almost like a machine.
'Bart, Dimar... stand accused of conducting experiments banned by the Inquisition to satisfy their private desires, terrorizing the local population...'
'...sentenced to life in the Bastión de Cánticos for such heinous acts.'
These are...
The judgments... of those who participated in the project.
Hearing those names seems to bring about a change in the old clerk's voice.
'Dorren, Castro, Liam... bodies discovered in the Salt Flat after attempting to flee Iberia.'
Please review and sign—
'Clara...'

'Guilty of stealing Inquisition records and disseminating confidential experiment data without authorization... sentenced to ten years in the Bastión de Cánticos... died of illness during incarceration.'
Clara... that Liberi lady with the golden hair? I remember that you and her...
(Whispers) Pale gold.
What?
She had just come to the lab from Perdon. She was innocent, lively, pretty, and her cheer was infectious. Everyone wanted to talk to her.
She helped us organize our data, while secretly developing a hair dye out of the seaweed we used in our experiments...
I could always smell a faint aroma when she walked past, one that reminded me of... the sea.
She wasn't the kind of person they're saying she was, right?
She just wanted to preserve the lab's research, the things that everyone poured their hearts and souls into...
Does it matter?
The Inquisition needs justifications to shut down such a large research project. Whether they're true or not, nobody cares.
But she was your...
I'm lucky I wasn't implicated because of my relationship with Clara and your grandfather. The Inquisition gave me a path forward...
I-I'm very grateful to them.
Grateful?
Th-There is still much to do! Let's get back to the work at hand, Señorita.
(Softly) *Sigh*...
Very well.
The next thing to review is...
The main component of the lab's core project. In the original concept, it supported systems that could quickly sequence the genomes of marine creatures and create samples.
It... It's not supposed to exist, not anymore...
The old man finally moves away from the mountain of papers, taking the tiny component from Weedy.
Weedy sees his expression—disbelief, realization, shock, scorn, pain, sorrow... A thousand emotions fill the face that was blank a moment ago.
'Disaster-bringing research'... 'corrupter of hearts'... 'beacon for the tides'...
So the Inquisition never destroyed the thing they called disaster-bringing research... They wanted me to see it—no, for you to see it again...
What are they thinking?!
Are you alright?
Are you still unwilling to talk, Señor?
What?
I don't care what the Inquisition intends. Temptation, scrutiny, control—Iberians have long been used to such things...
What I care about is you, Señor.
I don't think you're just an emotionless puppet. From the moment you stepped into this lab, I'd been waiting...
Waiting to truly meet you again.
Señorita...
Don't worry, Leaf has already confirmed that there's no one else here.
I—I'm here to send you away from Iberia.
The old man grabs Weedy's sleeve and gazes straight into her eyes. His eyes are sharp and strong, as though he's become a different person.
You should not have come back.
We were fortunate to have connections in the Inquisition, which allowed Señor Penia to get advanced warning. He leveraged all the connections he had to get you out of Iberia...
With dignity.
Yeah.
I'd wanted to leave Iberia and see what was outside. I remember it being a smooth process, but the Inquisitor who processed my documents said it would be hard to come back once I left.
None of that matters anymore.
Do not believe the finshit the Inquisitors tell you... 'That era is in the past'?
No, it's not. Even if land and sea have joined hands again, even if your company is in a position to do business in Iberia.
The Inquisition, their arrogance and tyranny, their cruelty and hypocrisy... None of it has changed.
Look at all these scrolls and records, this component that should have been destroyed...
I have no doubt now. Once you finish your business with Rhodes Island, they will demand that you forget everything that's happened, and that you restart the bionics research.
As though—*cough *cough*—as though the crimes they committed, the shame and despair we felt, as though none of that ever existed!
Please, calm down. Are you alright?
That's why, when that desgraciado told me you'd returned and ordered me to assist you, I knew I must send you away again!
The old man ignores Weedy's words and keeps talking.
All the years I've spent on my knees have broken them, Señorita, but I've gotten a few things out of this...
Before I came, I spent my last savings to get my hands on some forged official letters that will get you past the checkpoints, and buttered up the powers that be...
You will leave Iberia tonight.
What about you?
You can't fool the Inquisition. It won't be long until they find out.
None of it matters, as long as you're away from this country.
But the Inquisition will have your head!
No, Señorita Weedy—I will have THEIR heads.
Bart, Dimar...
Dorren, Castro, Liam...
Clara... oh, dear Clara...
And your grandfather, Señor Penia... The lab is no more. Our science is no more. All that's left is a reputation in tatters...
And an old man by the name of Callisto who yet lives, guarding these ruins.
I've been waiting for a chance!
You mean, me?
I'll send you away, and wait for the alguacil and the Inquisitors to come here and draw their swords at me in anger, just like they once did!
Then—*cough* then...
I will spit my blood on the faces of those malditos one last time!
The old man screams until his voice is rasp, but he continues to clutch the component in its hand. Its sharp edges pierce his palms, which have become red with blood.
But the man continues to rage, as though it is the only emotion his feeble body can house.
As though this emotion has kept him alive all these years.
Promise me, Señorita!
I promise, Señor Callisto.
I'll go.
And once you're gone, never return again.
Get on, Señorita. I must get back to the lab. The Inquisition will be there any moment...
Alright... Leaf!
Pack up Señor Callisto and put him in the trunk... carefully.
L-Let me go—what is the meaning of this?
The money and the letters are right next to you. I've talked to the coachman, who will take a little detour, where you'll be met by a colleague of mine...
A Liberi with a bright smile and a joking attitude, with a red streak in his white hair.
He'll send you back to your old home... the town of Luarca you used to tell me about, on the fringes of the Salt Flat, where people dance around a bonfire at night.
You can't do this! You promised me at the lab!
...Sorry, I lied.
If I didn't, you'd have gone and found an Inquisitor to fight to the death, wouldn't you?
I'm an operator of Rhodes Island. Our continued existence depends on this handover. I must remain in Iberia to complete my mission.
Whatever the Inquisition meant by 'vetting', I'll find out myself.
Señorita—Weedy—girl! My body is like a piece of withered wood! I don't have many years left! Just let me fulfill this last wish...
Exactly! You don't have many years left.
Don't you realize, Señor? It's not just the Inquisition that's imprisoned you. It's also you yourself.
I still remember hearing you talk about why you joined the lab—the way you imagined massive bionic fins that would let us freely sail the seas...
But now, your memories contain only pain and hatred.
I want you to go home, even if you only have the time to taste the briny winds of the Salt Flat, to watch the saltfins leap from the salt...
To talk to the young people dancing around the fire...
To sleep soundly on a rocking chair...
I want you to live your last days in peace.

Let this vehicle bring the story of Penia Lab and everything my grandfather directed to a close, whether it's the sin the Inquisition claims it was, or the miscarriage of justice you believe it to be.
You'll just let it go? Just like that?
Say goodbye to Señor Callisto, Leaf.
The bionic seadragon sways in front of the old man as though it is dancing.
This is...
Could this be... a bionic seadragon...
Mhm.
It pales in comparison to what your team once achieved, but Leaf is indeed a product of bionic technology.
Science does not end because someone rejects it, nor does it depend on being recognized to continue.
This is my way, and how I'll talk to them.
Adios, Señor.
Weedy takes a couple of steps back and pats the vehicle.
—Now go, Coachman.
The old man says no more. Leaning against the interior of the vehicle, he gazes out the window at Weedy and the land behind her, until it all grows distant and blurred.
He gazes blankly, as though he has never known the girl, delicate yet strong; as though he has never known this land, never known... himself.
Let's go, Leaf.
We have a lot to do.
Doña Irene.
Yes?
Señorita Weedy has made a last-minute demand...
She wants the Inquisition to promise not to pursue the case of Señor Callisto?
Yes.
I see no reason to refuse.
It seems you've misunderstood something.
Wh-What is it, Doña?
Vetting is indeed crucial for this handover of the Rhodes Island Catastrophe warning system and medical center core components, for it is of great importance to both land and sea.
But it is not just Operator Weedy of Rhodes Island who is being put to the test. You and I, and the Inquisition itself... we are all being tested. Think about it.
...How we should face the past, and how we should approach the future in this new era.
Wrap up the vetting process for Operator Weedy. She has demonstrated that she is more than just the descendant of a sinner, or an obsessed scientist.
Understood.
